name: Kt/V
seoDesc: Kt/V: work out URR from the pre-dialysis BUN and the post-dialysis BUN. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply the pre-dialysis BUN, the post-dialysis BUN, the duration of dialysis and the volume of removed ultrafiltrate and the Kt/V calculator solves for URR. Think of it as a shortcut for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the Kt/V calculator work?
sections.html:
The Kt/V calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports URR in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the pre-dialysis BUN, the post-dialysis BUN, the duration of dialysis and the volume of removed ultrafiltrate.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Kt/V calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

URR=(-post-dialysis BUN + pre-dialysis BUN) ÷ pre-dialysis BUN
Post-dialysis weight=(1 ÷ 2) × volume of removed ultrafiltrate × (-7 × post-dialysis BUN + 8 × pre-dialysis BUN) ÷ (pre-dialysis BUN × (kt ÷ V + the natural log of ((1 ÷ 125) × (-duration of dialysis × pre-dialysis BUN + 125 × post-dialysis BUN) ÷ pre-dialysis BUN)))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• Shown in percent, and convertible to any of the 6 units on that chip.
  • Shown in kilograms, and convertible to any of the 29 units on that chip.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Bun – blood urea nitrogen, opening in milligrams per deciliter
  • Bun – blood urea nitrogen, opening in milligrams per deciliter
  • Time, opening in hours
  • Volume, opening in liters
  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • %, opening in percent

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Kt/V calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the pre-dialysis BUN, the post-dialysis BUN and the duration of dialysis — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Kt/V calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns URR, derived from the pre-dialysis BUN, the post-dialysis BUN and the duration of dialysis. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Kt/V calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the pre-dialysis BUN, the post-dialysis BUN, the duration of dialysis and the volume of removed ultrafiltrate, which is 5 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter pre-dialysis BUN in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Pre-dialysis BUN opens in milligrams per deciliter and the chip beside it offers 2 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the Kt/V calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
